context:
Goal: sessions stop each other only when that is safe and meant.
Problem (rule): auto mode refused `mcp__claude-code-remote__interrupt_session` from a record-writer agent in lane roles-follow-ruling (2026-11-01 22:25 CST). The call was stray: the brief asked for no interrupt, so nothing was lost.
Based on (ruling): decision auto-mode-owner-acts keeps `priority: now`, which interrupts the target's running turn, out of "Owner Session Message". Asked because the interrupt_session tool itself is named in no ruling.
Departs from: main, where auto mode refuses interrupt_session. Option a adds an allow entry.

options.gain: A coordinator can stop a lane that has gone off track without asking you.
options.label: Allow interrupt_session for a session that started the target
options.lose: A stray interrupt, like the one on 2026-11-01, would go through and cut a lane's turn.

options.gain: No session cuts another's turn by mistake. It matches the decision that keeps `priority: now` out.
options.label: Keep it refused; the note closes with this ruling (recommended)
options.lose: You stop a stuck lane yourself.

reply: Dropped: decision report-guard-refusal-right (2026-11-01) already rules that when auto mode rightly refuses a stray agent call such as interrupt_session, the refusal stays and no allow-tool question is filed. The note interrupt-session-refused closes under that decision.
title: Should auto mode allow a session to interrupt another session?
why: Kept note interrupt-session-refused asks you to say whether to allow the tool. The coordinator asked for it at 14:32 CST.
